result.note: Tests the safe harbour amendment, the February 2026 takedown window change and the AI Impact Summit venue.

questions.prompt: In March 2026, India proposed amendments to its IT rules concerning internet platforms. Consider the following statements:
items: Safe harbour is the legal shield that protects platforms from liability for user-posted content.
Under the rules in force before the proposal, IT ministry advisories on deepfake labelling were already legally binding on platforms.
The proposed amendment would treat non-compliance with ministry advisories as a failure to meet safe harbour conditions.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Under the current rules, the IT ministry's advisories function as guidance without legal teeth, and the proposal seeks to make them binding by linking them to safe harbour. The draft rules were published for public feedback, with comments open until 14 April 2026.
questions.source: The proposed amendment would treat non-compliance as a failure to meet safe harbour conditions, the legal shield that protects platforms from liability for user-posted content.

questions.prompt: In February 2026, the Union government shortened the window within which internet platforms must take down flagged content. The window was reduced from 36 hours to:
questions.explain: The takedown window was compressed from 36 hours to three hours. At the same time, new disclosure and metadata requirements were introduced for AI-generated content.
questions.source: In February, the Modi government compressed the content takedown window from 36 hours to three hours

questions.prompt: In February 2026, the AI Impact Summit, attended by the heads of Google, OpenAI and Anthropic, was held in which city?
questions.explain: Sundar Pichai, Sam Altman and Dario Amodei all attended the summit in New Delhi. Global AI companies are competing for Indian users, with free offers and bundling deals with telecom operators Airtel and Jio.
questions.source: At the AI Impact Summit in February, Sundar Pichai, Sam Altman, and Dario Amodei all showed up in New Delhi.
